claims.claim_text: Email's median first response rose from 95 minutes in April to 131 minutes in June.
The share of email tickets resolved within 24 hours fell from 71% in April to 64% in June.
Across the quarter, email's median first response was 95 minutes against 5 minutes for chat and 3 minutes for phone, and its median satisfaction score was 3.90 against 4.20 and 4.40.
Chat handled 655 tickets in April and 748 in June while its median first response stayed between 4 and 6 minutes.
Email tickets rose from 398 in May to 451 in June.
Two email agents moved to the chat queue at the start of June.
Chat moved to a 7x24 schedule in April 2026, while email and phone are staffed on weekdays only.
Customer satisfaction comes from a post-ticket survey that fewer than one in five customers answer.
Ticket counts do not separate new customers from existing ones.
The mean of the three channels' median first response rose from 33.67 minutes in April to 46.67 minutes in June, while the median across channels moved only from 4 to 6 minutes.
The ticket sheet and memo use illustrative figures prepared for a training exercise.
A billing change on 3 June produced a spike of email questions about invoices.
